name: badge
description: UIDS badge component contract, preserving the verified 4.x rendering and documenting the proposed Figma representation.

figma.note: BUILT (Phase 3). 6 variants on one axis: Type (Primary, Secondary, Cool Gray, Blue, Green, Orange). Nothing to collapse — Badge has one enum option and one content prop, so the naive count already equals the achievable minimum. The simplest set in the library.
axisRationale: Labels use Title Case, spacing the one two-word value ('Cool Gray'), matching the existing Button Color axis convention (Primary/Secondary/Tertiary).

No Style or Size axis is needed the way Button (144 -> 27) or Headline (Level x Style = 30) required. A size modifier was DECLINED on 2026-08-21 (see changes[2]), so Type is the complete axis list, not a first instalment — do not add a Size axis to the set in anticipation of one.

options.name: type
options.description: Colorway. Drives one BEM modifier class; primary is the only value that also overrides text color (to black) — every other value keeps the base white text.

code.notes: Badge.vue:6-16 defineProps validator restricts to exactly these 6 strings (matches Badge.stories.js argTypes.type.options exactly, and matches the 6 badge--* selectors defined in badge.scss — no drift in any direction).

options.name: text
options.description: Required content string, rendered verbatim as the badge's only visible content (Badge.vue:34, {{ text }}). NOT a <slot> — Badge has no slot of its own, unlike every other migrated component (Button/Headline both wrap a default slot). Vue marks it required:true with no default (Badge.vue:18-21); omitting it is a runtime prop-validation warning, not a build error.

figma.notes: Modelled as a text layer bound to the badge instance, the same role Button/Headline give their default slot's Label/Text property — the difference is code-side only (prop vs. slot), not a Figma-modelling difference.

behavior: Exactly one modifier class is ever applied alongside the base .badge: Badge.vue's computed `classes` always resolves to ['badge', `badge--${type}`] (Badge.vue:24-29). There is no code path that renders .badge alone, with more than one modifier, or with a modifier outside the validator's 6 values.

Only badge--primary overrides text color, to black/$blk (badge.scss:17). badge--secondary/--cool-gray/--blue/--green/--orange (badge.scss:20-38) declare only `background` — none sets `color` — so all five inherit the base .badge white text color (badge.scss:10).

Badge has no <slot>; content flows through the required `text` string prop, interpolated directly (Badge.vue:34). Figma should still bind the instance's Text layer to this value the way it would a slot-based label — see the `text` option's figma notes.

The badge renders at ONE size everywhere. font-size is an absolute 0.75rem ({typography.font-size.25}) as of 2026-08-20 — see changes[0] — so a badge in an h1, a table cell and a body paragraph all measure the same 12px type, 9px inline padding, 12px radius and 20.04px line box. padding-inline (.75em) and border-radius (1em) remain em-relative, but they now resolve against a fixed base, so they are proportional to the badge's own type rather than to its surroundings. That geometry is what would make a size modifier cheap — setting font-size alone moves the whole pill — but one was DECLINED on 2026-08-21 (see changes[2]); this sentence records the mechanism, not a plan.
changes: 2026-08-20 — BADGE NO LONGER FLEXES WITH ITS CONTEXT. badge/font-size went from a raw "75%" of the INHERITED font-size to an absolute {typography.font-size.25} = 0.75rem. The design system owner's ruling: "I don't want badges to flex to a larger size inside headings. So we need to make that change across all contexts. If we want badge sizing we can introduce modifier sizing." A DELIBERATE DESIGN CHANGE, a departure from tokenize-as-shipped -- NOT a fidelity bug to fix back. Impact is asymmetric: 0.75rem is what 75% resolved to at 1rem, so body copy, table cells and card meta are pixel-unchanged; headings stop growing. padding-inline and border-radius stay em, so the pill follows the badge's own type, now resolving to a fixed 9px and 12px. Consequences: the Figma rebind (changes[3]), the smoke test (knownIssues), the size modifier the ruling leaves open -- DECLINED 2026-08-21, changes[2].

2026-08-20 — the readme composition rule 'Never put a Badge inside a heading' and the contracts/rules.json badge-inline-only clause 'To flag a whole block, put the badge inside that block's heading or first line' were direct opposites, both shipped. The change above makes a badge in a heading render correctly, so the prohibition is retired and badge-inline-only was rewritten to state what remains true: a badge is an inline pill at a fixed size, never absolutely positioned, floated, or mounted as a corner flag.

2026-08-21 — SIZE MODIFIER DECLINED; the badge is one fixed size. The design system owner's ruling: "no badge modifier, just a fixed size badge for now." This CLOSES the question changes[0] left open. The badge renders at 0.75rem / 12px type in every context, with the 9px padding and 12px radius that follow; there is no `size` option, no Size axis, nothing queued. Recorded rather than left as silence because the absence must read as deliberate: a later agent meeting a one-size badge next to Button's Small/Medium/Large would otherwise take it for an oversight and "add the missing sizes" — exactly the re-litigation this array prevents. This entry moves no pixels — it declines a proposal rather than altering rendering — so the contract version does not move with it. Reopening needs a fresh ruling from the design system owner, still contract-first: a size modifier expands public shape.

2026-08-21 — THE FIGMA REBIND IS DONE AND THE UNBOUND-9PX ISSUE IS CLOSED. Two jobs, both done: three Component variables were corrected: badge/font-size stopped being a raw 75 (a leftover from `font-size: 75%`) now ALIASES a new Primitives variable font/size/25 = 12, badge/padding/inline went 12 -> 9, badge/border-radius 16 -> 12, the values `.75em` and `1em` resolve to against the 0.75rem base (changes[0]) — then all six variants were bound: padding -> badge/padding/inline, four radii -> badge/border-radius, text fontSize -> badge/font-size. NOTHING MOVED: the frames already PAINTED 9, 12 and 12 as raw literals under the 2026-08-16 "visual truth wins in a design library" ruling, so before and after are identical on every geometry field, closing the gap between what the file showed and what it could prove. check-figma went 11 errors to 0. It REPLACES a knownIssue: that defect is closed.
knownIssues: Dead import: `@use '../abstracts/utilities'` (badge.scss:2) — the `utilities` namespace is never referenced anywhere in the file. See claims.

`border: 1px solid transparent` (badge.scss:11) is never overridden by any of the 6 modifiers — its color channel has no observable visual effect in any shipped variant. See claims. Not tokenized (see geometryNotTokenized).

type='orange' maps to the $danger Sass variable / {color.status.danger} primitive (#BD472A), NOT a literal orange hue — already precedented in tokens/primitives/colors.json's own comment ('4.x: $danger / $orange'). Must be spelled out explicitly in the eventual contract's option description so it doesn't read as a naming error, same treatment as Button's dead 'link' color value.

type='blue' maps to the $info Sass variable / {color.status.info} primitive (#00558C) — a status-semantic color, not the separate {color.blue} 'link blue' primitive that happens to share the exact same current hex value. This is a sharper version of the orange mismatch above: picking {color.blue} instead of {color.status.info} would look identical today and only reveal itself as wrong if the two primitives are ever retuned independently. Flag explicitly in the contract; do not rely on the numeric coincidence.

uids_base (downstream, /Users/bspeare/acquia/uiowa) defines a 7th modifier not present in Badge.vue's validator or badge.scss: `.badge--light { background: $light; color: $secondary; }` (uids_base/scss/components/badge.scss:5-8, gray-100 background / black text by default theme). A repo-wide grep of uiowa (scss/twig/php/js) found no static or programmatic caller for the class — it may be reachable only via manually-authored WYSIWYG markup, which repo grep cannot see. Same treatment as Button's circle/caps/lowercase: a live-in-the-consumer, public-shape-expansion candidate, deferred past this migration and owned by uids_base today, NOT a dead-code claim (the rule itself is fully functional if invoked).

DOWNSTREAM SMOKE TEST OWED for the 2026-08-20 sizing change (changes[0]): uids_base overrides the base `.badge` selector (display:inline-flex, plus a Font Awesome margin rule) and adds a 7th `.badge--light` modifier. Neither is UIDS's to change here, but both sit on top of the selector whose font-size just became absolute, so whoever owns uiowa/uiowa should confirm no downstream caller relied on badges scaling with their container.

uids_base also overrides the base `.badge` selector itself (uids_base/scss/components/badge.scss:10-16): `display: inline-flex` (UIDS ships `inline-block`, badge.scss:5) plus a nested `.svg-inline--fa { margin-right: .4rem; align-self: center; }` rule sized for a Font Awesome icon that Badge.vue has no slot or prop to render. No live badge+icon markup was found by repo grep in either repo, so this may be defensive/anticipatory CSS. UIDS's own `inline-block` remains the correct canonical value for this contract (it is what Storybook renders and what the regression baseline captures); the uids_base override is downstream and out of scope here, but a future icon-slot addition to Badge.vue should reconcile with it.

`uids_base/uids/scss/components/badge.scss` is a byte-identical vendored mirror of this repo's badge.scss (diffed clean) — a downstream artifact, not a second implementation; recorded in identity.downstreamPaths for traceability, not treated as drift.

The 6 `badge--{type}` class strings are hardcoded literals in production code well beyond Vue/Storybook: e.g. facilities.uiowa.edu's UtilityAlertsController.php, registrar's AcademicCalendarController.php and CourseDeadlinesForm.php, its.uiowa.edu's AlertTypeLegend.php, uiowa_hours' HoursFilterForm.php, and raw JS in admissions/pharmacy counselors-map.js. The 6 enum values are a de facto public API consumed by PHP controllers and inline JS, not just the Vue prop — renaming or removing any of them is a breaking change for those call sites.

geometryNotTokenized.border: 1px solid transparent (badge.scss:11). Width is hardcoded per the Border foundation's own convention (contracts/border.json: '1px solid is hardcoded... not tokenized'); the color is the literal CSS keyword `transparent`, never overridden by any modifier (see claims), so there is no meaningful color value to reference either — the rule reserves 1px of box size without ever painting a visible border.
